title: The Definite Integral as a Limit of Sums and as Signed Area
quickIdea: The definite integral is the limit of a sum of thin rectangles, and its value is net signed area: area above the axis counts positive, area below counts negative.
remember: Definition: the integral from a to b of f(x) dx is the limit as n grows of the sum of f(x_i*) times the width of each of n equal subintervals. It exists when f is continuous on [a, b].
The value is a number, not a function: the variable x is a dummy, so the integral of f(t) dt from a to b is the same number.
The integral from a to a is 0, because the width is zero - whatever the height.
The lower limit need not be smaller than the upper limit; the definition still works and the sign rule below fixes the meaning.

If f is at least 0 on [a, b] then the integral is at least 0; if f is at most 0 then the integral is at most 0. Equality to zero happens either when the width is zero or when the signed pieces cancel.
Area and integral differ exactly when the curve crosses the axis: the area is the integral of |f|, the integral is the integral of f.

example.prompt: Evaluate the integral of 2x from 0 to 1 from the definition, then confirm it by area.
example.work: An antiderivative of 2x is x^2, so the value is 1^2 - 0^2 = 1. Geometrically the graph of y = 2x from x = 0 to x = 1 is a right triangle with base 1 and height 2, and its area is (1/2)(1)(2) = 1.

gateAngle: The signed-area reading is what GATE tests when a function changes sign on the interval: 2014 Set 3 Q.6 asks for the integral of |x sin x| over [0, 2pi] and the modulus is there precisely so that the negative piece counts positive. 2015 Set 2 Q.26 turns the same distinction into a three-statement question about whether the area of an unbounded function is finite.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: The integral of x from -1 to 1 is 0. What is the area between y = x and the x-axis on [-1, 1]?
variations.why: The integral is the net signed area: the triangle below the axis on [-1, 0] has area 1/2 and counts -1/2, the triangle above on [0, 1] has area 1/2 and counts +1/2, and they cancel. The area is the integral of |x|, which is 1. GATE words this as 'area bounded by the curve and the x-axis'.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: If the integral of f from 0 to 2 is 5 and f is continuous and positive on [0, 2], what can you say about the integral of f from 2 to 0?
variations.why: Reversing the limits reverses the sign, because every rectangle's width changes sign. The positivity of f is irrelevant to this property; it only tells you the forward integral is positive.

trap.what: Reporting the signed integral when the question asks for the area, or assuming a zero integral means zero area.
trap.why: The integral adds signed rectangles; the area adds their absolute values. They agree only when the integrand keeps one sign on the interval.
trap.counterexample: On [0, 2pi] the integral of x sin x is -2pi, while the area between |x sin x| and the axis is 4pi - the two differ by the sign of the piece from pi to 2pi, and GATE CSE 2014 Set 3 Q.6 asks for the second of these.

check.question: A function is positive on [0, 1] and negative on [1, 2], and its integral from 0 to 1 equals minus its integral from 1 to 2. What is its integral from 0 to 2?
check.explanation: Additivity gives the integral over [0, 2] as the sum of the two pieces, and they are exact opposites. The area is not zero: it is twice the size of one piece, which is the point of the trap above.
